objective.statement: Group the notes and rests of an irregular bar so that they show the stated grouping.
successCriteria: I beam each group of two or three separately.
I never let a note or a rest cross from one group into the next.
I check the total, the grouping and the beams as three separate things.

explanation.text: In an irregular bar each group is written as if it were a bar of its own: just as it would be if it were a complete group of two or three beats. There are no special rules beyond that. A group of three quavers is joined by one beam; a group of two is joined by another; the beams never join notes from two different groups.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 5/8. The first is grouped three then two; the second is grouped two then three.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver), 2 beamed together (quaver, quaver). Bar 2: 2 beamed together (quaver, quaver), 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver).

explanation.caption: The same five quavers: 3 + 2 in the first bar, 2 + 3 in the second.

explanation.text: A bar that adds up is not necessarily a bar that is grouped well. Check three things one at a time. First, the total: does the bar add up to the signature? Second, the grouping: do the groups match the pattern asked for? Third, the notation: are the beams and rests grouped inside each group?

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 5/4: a dotted minim then a minim (3 + 2), then three crotchets and a minim (3 + 2).
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted minim, minim. Bar 2: crotchet, crotchet, crotchet, minim.

explanation.caption: In 5/4 the groups are shown by note lengths: nothing crosses from beat 3 into beat 4.

explanation.text: Rests follow the same idea. A whole group may be one rest, and a single beat may be one rest; a rest that begins in one group and ends in another is not used. Questions always say which grouping is wanted, so you never have to guess.
Name the grouping first (for example 2 + 3), then fill or beam one group at a time, left to right.

mistakes.beam-across-middle: Count how many notes each beam joins: those numbers are the grouping.
mistakes.rest-across-beat: That rest hides where a beat begins. Use one rest to finish the beat, and another for the next.
mistakes.half-bar-rest-misplaced: A two-beat rest can fill the first or second half of a four-beat bar, but not the middle two beats.
mistakes.tie-instead-of-dot: A dotted note says the same thing more simply here.
mistakes.compound-beat-hidden: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Mark where each beat starts, then regroup.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 05, drafted with AI assistance; pending qualified teacher review)
provenance.notes: Original wording. First Steps Grade 5 section 1 (p. 105): no special rules; each subdivision of an irregular bar is grouped in the usual way. Beamed grouping is read in x/8 only (OPEN_QUESTIONS Q30/Q35); rests fill a whole group or one unit. Every question names the wanted grouping, as the brief requires.
